items.title: 7.3 The Digital Divide and Its Impacts

blocks.title: Digital divide
blocks.text: The digital divide is the gap between people, communities and regions that have access to modern information and communication technology (ICT) and those that do not, in internet access, devices and digital literacy.
It matters because it leads to unequal opportunities in education, jobs, healthcare and social participation.

blocks.alt: Top: three columns, causes of the digital divide (economic, geographical, educational, social), its impacts (education, jobs, civic life, health, digital literacy) and bridges (Universal Service Fund, literacy programmes, partnerships), joined by arrows. Bottom left: a seven-item checklist for judging a source. Bottom right: habits of a good digital citizen.
blocks.caption: The digital divide, judging sources and digital citizenship (original diagram after topics 7.3 to 7.6).
blocks.long_description: The digital divide is caused by cost, lack of rural networks, low digital skills and social barriers such as age, gender and disability; it widens gaps in education, jobs, civic participation, health and digital literacy; and it can be bridged by government projects such as the Universal Service Fund, literacy programmes and public-private partnerships. Before trusting information, check who published it, their authority, the data's origin, whether it is a primary source, other viewpoints, red flags and bias. A good digital citizen uses strong passwords, avoids suspicious links, shares data carefully, respects copyright, uses privacy settings, collaborates and makes content accessible.

blocks.prompt: Name three forms the digital divide can take.
blocks.explanation: Unequal access to the internet, to computing devices, and to digital literacy (skills).

items: Digital divide: unequal access to ICT, devices and skills, causing unequal opportunities.
